title: Utilizing Wearable Technology for Enhanced Monitoring and Management
summary: The main project goal is to investigate whether continuous real-time monitoring through wearables can effectively predict Post-Exertional Malaise (PEM) and associated "crashes" in individuals with Post-COVID Syndrome (PCS). These insights will then be used to develop interventions. The focus is on examining the relationships between physiological parameters captured by wearables and the PEM symptoms reported by patients. Based on these individual real-time data, models will be developed using machine learning to predict PEM-associated crashes. Data collection will occur in three groups: PCS patients with PEM, patients with inflammatory rheumatic diseases and PEM, and a healthy control group. This approach not only allows for the characterization of PEM patterns in PCS but also enables comparison with other conditions where PEM occurs.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
informed consent, proficiency in using mobile devices, mild to severe fatigue symptoms, PEM (except the healthy controls)
Exclusion criteria:
Other severe health impairments that severely reduced physical activity even before PEM.
